:::{#thm-similar-eigenvalues}
#### Similar matrices have the same eigenvalues

If $\matr{B} = \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P}$ (@def-similar),
then $\vecf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $\matr{A}$ for $\eigval$
exactly when $\matr{P}^{-1} \vecf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $\matr{B}$ for $\eigval$.
So $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$ have the same eigenvalues.

:::

::: proof

**From $\matr{A}$ to $\matr{B}$.**
Let $\matr{A} \vecf{v} = \eigval \vecf{v}$ with $\vecf{v} \ne \vzero$, and $\vecf{w} = \matr{P}^{-1} \vecf{v}$. Then

$$
\ba
\matr{B} \vecf{w}
&= (\matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P})\,(\matr{P}^{-1} \vecf{v})
&& \text{(substitute } \matr{B} \text{ and } \vecf{w} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A}\,(\matr{P} \matr{P}^{-1})\,\vecf{v}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A}\,\matr{I}_p\,\vecf{v}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-inverse)}
\\
&= \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \vecf{v}
&& \text{(@thm-identity)}
\\
&= \matr{P}^{-1}\,(\matr{A} \vecf{v})
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \matr{P}^{-1}\,(\eigval \vecf{v})
&& \text{(eigenvector)}
\\
&= \eigval\,\vecf{w}.
&& \text{(@thm-scalar-matmul)}
\ea
$$

And $\vecf{w} \ne \vzero$: if $\vecf{w} = \vzero$, then
$\vecf{v} = \matr{I}_p \vecf{v} = \matr{P}\,(\matr{P}^{-1} \vecf{v}) = \matr{P}\,\vzero = \vzero$
(@thm-identity, @def-matrix-inverse, @thm-matmul-assoc, @def-matvec-mult),
which is false.

**From $\matr{B}$ to $\matr{A}$.**
By @rem-similar-both-ways, $\matr{A} = \matr{P} \matr{B} \matr{P}^{-1} = (\matr{P}^{-1})^{-1} \matr{B}\,\matr{P}^{-1}$,
so the first part, with $\matr{P}^{-1}$ in place of $\matr{P}$ and the roles of $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$ exchanged,
shows that if $\vecf{w} = \matr{P}^{-1} \vecf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $\matr{B}$ for $\eigval$,
then $\matr{P} \vecf{w}$ is an eigenvector of $\matr{A}$ for $\eigval$;
and $\matr{P} \vecf{w} = \matr{P} \matr{P}^{-1} \vecf{v} = \vecf{v}$
(@thm-matmul-assoc, @def-matrix-inverse, @thm-identity).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-similar-eigenvalues}
#### Eigenvectors carried across a similarity

In @exm-similar, $\matr{B} = \diag(3, 1)$ has eigenvectors $(1, 0)$ for $3$ and $(0, 1)$ for $1$:
$\diag(3, 1)\,(1, 0) = (3, 0)$ and $\diag(3, 1)\,(0, 1) = (0, 1)$.
$\matr{P}\,(1, 0) = (1, 1)$ and $\matr{P}\,(0, 1) = (1, -1)$
are the eigenvectors of $\matr{A}$ for $3$ and $1$ found in @exm-eigenvalue.

:::
